segments.text: Listening Test In the listening test, you will be asked
to demonstrate how well you understand spoken English.
The entire listening test will last approximately 45 minutes.
There are four parts and directions are given for each part.
You must mark your answers on the separate answer sheet.
Do not write your answers in your test book.
Part 1.
Directions For each question in this part, you will
hear four statements about a picture in your test book.
When you hear the statements, you must select the one statement that best describes what
you see in the picture.
Then find the number of the question on your answer sheet and mark your answer.
The statements will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Now part 1 will begin.
Number 1.
Look at the picture marked number 1 in your test book.
A.
Some notebooks are stacked on a desk.
B.
A drawer is being opened.
C.
A lamp is covered with folders.
Some pens are scattered across a desk.
Number 2.
Look at the picture marked number 2 in your test book.
A.
Shopping carts are being pushed through a store.
C.
Groceries have been placed in a cart.
D.
Some shopping carts are lined up near an entrance.
Number 3.
Look at the picture marked number 3 in your test book.
A.
One of the men is holding a broom.
B.
One of the men is climbing a ladder.
C.
The men are carrying a board.
D.
The men are painting a wall.
Number 4.
Look at the picture marked number 4 in your test book.
A.
He's watering a plant.
B.
He's opening a door.
C.
He's pushing a chair.
D.
He's vacuuming a carpet.
Number 5.
Look at the picture marked number 5 in your test book.
A.
She's stacking some folders on a desk.
B.
She's refilling a printer with paper.
C.
Some folders have been dropped on the floor.
D.
A printer is positioned on a cabinet.
Number 6.
Look at the picture marked number 6 in your test book.
A.
The cabinet has been left open.
B.
Mugs have been placed on a counter.
C.
The coffee machine is being cleaned.
D.
Napkins have been stacked on a chair.
Part 2.
Directions.
You will hear a question or statement and three responses spoken in English.
They will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Select the best response to the question or statement and mark the letter A, B or C
on your answer sheet.
Now, let us begin with question number 7.
Number 7.
When can I pick up my dog after the operation?
A.
About $180.
B.
Has the vet finished checking on her yet?
C.
In the recovery room at the back.
Number 8.
How many jars of the wildflower honey do you have left?
A.
Yes, the bees were very busy this year.
B.
Only about 4, I think.
C.
Sure, I'll set some aside for you.
Number 9.
Who's presenting the traffic report this hour?
A.
No, the microphone's working fine.
B.
Isn't it written on the schedule board?
C.
The report covers the highway closures.
Number 10.
How often do the tour boats leave the dark?
A.
Every half hour or so?
B.
The boat ride was wonderful.
C.
Yes, from the north pier.
Number 11.
Why can't we stay open later on Fridays?
A.
Right by the front entrance?
B.
The new display goes up Saturday.
C.
Because we're short on evening staff.
Number 12.
How do I sign up for the rewards card?
A.
He's collecting his award.
B.
They're next to the registers.
Do you have our app?
Number 13.
Has the irrigation system been repaired yet?
A.
The report's already prepared.
B.
A technician's coming this afternoon.
C.
Water the plants every morning.
Number 14.
Who's driving the airport shuttle this evening?
A.
Every 20 minutes.
B.
Bernard is.
C.
The evening flight's arriving.
Number 15.
When are the new laptops being handed out to everyone?
A.
Sometime next week I heard B.
Because the shipment got delayed.
C.
No, I already knew about it.
Number 16.
The cough syrups out of stock, isn't it?
A.
Everything's kept in the stockroom out back.
B.
It's for treating a sore throat.
C.
Yes, but we can have it in by tomorrow.
Number 17.
Who has the keys to the delivery van?
A.
The vases are in the back.
B.
Gavin took them earlier.
Sometime after the noon deliveries.
Number 18.
Do you know whether these cardboard boxes can be recycled here?
A.
You'd have to ask the attendant over there.
B.
The recycling bins are emptied every morning.
C.
Yes, I flattened them before I came.
Number 19.
What did you think of the new spin class?
A.
Over by the water fountain.
B.
No, I already knew that.
C.
I thought it was pretty intense.
Number 20.
Is the crew going to finish clearing the fallen tree today?
Or will they have to come back another day?
A.
It's a pretty big oak.
About 40 feet tall.
B.
She's the supervisor for this job.
C.
They'll be back Thursday morning.
Number 21.
The Oakmont Gallery moved their exhibit opening up to Thursday.
A.
OK, I'll let the framers know.
The bottle opener is in the drawer.
C.
No, the movers haven't arrived yet.
Number 22.
One of the reading lamps at the corner study table keeps flickering.
A.
I'll grab a replacement bulb from the closet.
B.
The crick away in is past the front desk.
C.
Your library card's just been renewed.
Number 23.
Why is the lobby fountain switched off this morning?
A.
No, I haven't found it anywhere.
B.
The maintenance crew is draining it to clean the filter.
C.
Yes, the water was really cold.
Number 24.
Would you mind checking whether my room's ready yet?
A.
Sure, I'll have your bags taken up.
B.
The system's been down all morning.
C.
It's 120 a night.
Number 25.
Wasn't the guitar you tried out last month still for sale?
A.
They're along the far wall.
B.
No, I wasn't too tired that day.
C.
Actually, someone bought it on Saturday.
Number 26.
How do I book one of the private meeting rooms?
A.
The meeting starts at 3.
B.
They're listed in our member app.
C.
Yes, I booked it yesterday.
Number 27.
Who do you think has the best chance of winning the cook-off this year?
A.
They're all doing a great job this year.
B.
I actually won it two years ago.
C.
Sorry, I'm too full to try anymore.
Number 28.
Did Ms. Corrigan give you the delivery invoice?
A.
I thought she handed it to you.
B.
The invitations were mailed yesterday.
She's leaving early today.
Number 29.
Isn't the last fairy running tonight?
A.
Yes, it leaves at 9.
The fair went up last week.
C.
I'm having dinner beforehand.
Number 30.
Who approved the change to the new bottle supplier?
A.
The plant manager did, I believe.
B.
Sometime late last month, I think.
C.
No, the new bottles are a little taller.
Number 31.
The vendor grinds the beans fresh before he opens up each morning, doesn't he?
A.
Well, his grinder's been out for repair all week.
B.
Over by the bakery stall.
C.
No, I've been there twice.
Part 3.
Directions.
You will hear some conversations between two or more people.
You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation.
Select the best response to each question and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet.
The conversations will not be printed in your testbook and will be spoken only one time.
Questions 32 through 34 refer to the following conversation.
Good morning.
We still need to get our booth ready for the trade show and it opens tomorrow morning.
I know.
I've already packed the brochures and the display table is set up in the corner.
Great.
But the banner we ordered just arrived and it's the wrong size.
It's far too small for our booth.
Hmm.
I can call the supplier right now and ask them to reprint it overnight.
That would be perfect.
I have to go to a meeting with the sales team in a few minutes.
So could you handle that?
Of course.
I'll contact them and make sure the new banner is ready by this afternoon.
Number 32.
Where is the conversation most likely taking place?
Number 33.
What problem does the man mention?
Number 34.
Where will the man go next?
Questions 35 through 37 refer to the following conversation with three speakers.
Okay everyone, before we get started we've got a problem with this weekend.
The Saturday evening dinner service is short staffed.
Two people called in sick and I need at least one more person on the line.
Corinne, is there any chance you could come in?
I'd really like to help but I'm already scheduled for the Saturday lunch shift.
I'll have been here since 10 in the morning so I honestly can't stay for the evening as well.
Right, that's fair.
Theo, what about you?
Could you cover the dinner service instead?
Sure, I can do that.
The only thing is, I've got an appointment in the afternoon so I wouldn't be able to get here until about five o'clock.
As long as that's alright, I'm happy to help out.
Five is fine.
It doesn't get busy until later anyway.
Great, that solves it.
I'll go update the schedule on the board right now so everyone can see the change.
Number 35.
Where does the conversation most likely take place?
Number 36.
Why can't the woman work the evening shift?
Number 37.
What does the man say he will do next?
Questions 38 through 40 refer to the following conversation.
Good morning.
I've just arrived after a long trip and I was hoping to check into my room right now if that's at all possible.
I'd be glad to help you with that.
Unfortunately, your room isn't quite ready just yet.
Our housekeeping team doesn't finish cleaning the rooms until early afternoon, around two o'clock.
Oh, that's a bit later than I was expecting.
Is there anything I can do while I wait?
Maybe leave my thing somewhere?
Of course.
We can store your luggage behind the front desk at no charge.
And I'll also give you a complimentary voucher for our lobby cafe while you wait.
That works perfectly for me.
I'll leave my bags here with you then and go explore the area for a bit.
Number 38.
Where most likely are the speakers?
Number 39.
What problem does the woman mention?
Number 40.
What does the man say he will do?
Questions 41 through 43 refer to the following conversation.
Hi, good morning.
Welcome desk over here, right?
I'd like to have this suit cleaned, please.
The thing is, I'm flying out on a business trip Thursday morning, so I really need it back before then.
Of course, let me take a quick look.
Alright, for a wool suit like this one, our standard cleaning takes four business days.
So, if you leave it today, it would be ready next Monday afternoon.
Oh, Monday?
But that's after I've already left town.
I understand completely.
In that case, we do offer a same day service.
If you drop the suit off before noon, we can have it cleaned and ready for you by six o'clock this evening.
That sounds perfect.
Is there anything different about the same day option?
Or is it just the timing that changes?
It's exactly the same cleaning process.
Just done more quickly.
There is one thing, though.
The rush service adds an extra $15 to the regular price.
Number 41.
What does the woman want to do?
Number 42.
What does the woman mean when she says, but that's after I've already left town?
Number 43.
What does the man say about the same day service?
Questions 44-46 refer to the following conversation with three speakers.
Good morning, and welcome to Martin Office Interiors.
My name's Julian.
Are you looking for anything in particular today, or would you like me to show you around?
Good morning.
My colleague and I are setting up a new office for our team, so we need about a dozen desks.
We saw the Meridian desk on your website.
Do you carry that one here in the showroom?
We certainly do, and it's one of our most popular models.
The price is very reasonable for the quality you're getting.
Why don't we walk over to the display area so you can try out a few samples in person?
That sounds great.
Before we head over, though, if we place an order today, how soon can the desks actually be delivered?
For that particular model, delivery usually takes about five business days once the order is confirmed.
Perfect. Thanks very much.
Number 44.
Where are the speakers?
Number 45.
Where will the speakers most likely go next?
Number 46.
What does the woman ask about?
Questions 47-49 refer to the following conversation.
Hi, my name's Emil Vasquez.
I just finished my eye exam with the doctor a few minutes ago, and she said I could come over and pick out some new frames.
I'm hoping to find something nice and lightweight.
Of course. Welcome to Clearpoint Optical.
We've got a whole wall of lightweight metal frames right over here.
Before we start, may I ask what you'll mainly be using the new glasses for?
Mostly for work, actually.
I'm sitting at a computer screen pretty much all day, and my eyes always feel tired by the afternoon.
In that case, I'd really recommend adding an anti-glare coating to the lenses.
It cuts down the reflection you get from screens, so your eyes won't strain as much during those long days.
Oh, that sounds perfect.
Let's go ahead and add that.
And how soon will they be ready for me to collect?
With the extra coating, they take a little longer, so it'll be about a week.
Don't worry, though. We'll give you a call the moment they come in.
Number 47.
What is the reason for the man's visit to the shop?
Number 48.
What does the man say about his eyes?
Number 49.
Why does the woman recommend an added lens coating?
Questions 50 through 52 refer to the following conversation.
Hi. I have a personal training session booked with Curtis for this Thursday at 6 in the evening,
but I need to move it to a different day.
Some things come up with my work schedule.
I've got a meeting that afternoon that I just can't get out of.
No problem at all. Let me pull up Curtis's calendar for you.
Okay, so he's completely booked on Friday, but he does have openings on Saturday morning
and on Monday evening. Would either of those work for you?
Saturday morning would actually be perfect.
Could we do it around 10 o'clock?
10 o'clock on Saturday it is, Miss Eau Claire.
I'll update the booking right now and send you a confirmation by email.
And I'll make sure Curtis knows about the change as well.
Number 50.
Why is the woman at the desk?
Number 51.
Why does the woman need to change her booking?
Number 52.
What does the man say he will do?
Questions 53 through 55 refer to the following conversation.
Hi. This is Bridget Callahan.
I placed an order with your company for our office lunch this Friday,
and I'm calling because I'd like to change a couple of the dishes.
Of course. I have your order right here on my screen.
What would you like to adjust?
Well, when I ordered, I assumed everyone in my department eats meat,
but two people just told me they only eat plant-based meals.
Could we swap the chicken platters for some vegetarian options?
Let me see. Hmm, good news.
The kitchen hasn't started preparing anything for Friday yet.
Oh, that's a relief.
And while we're at it, could you add a tray of fresh fruit as well?
Absolutely. I'll update your order right now and email you a revised invoice within the hour.
Number 53.
What type of business does the man most likely work for?
Number 54.
Why does the man say the kitchen hasn't started preparing anything for Friday yet?
Number 55.
What does the man say he will do?
Questions 56-58 refer to the following conversation.
Hi. I'd like to order some fliers to advertise the opening of my shop.
I need about 500 of them, and the store opens this coming Saturday.
Is there any way you can have them ready by then?
Sure. 500 flyers is no problem at all.
Our standard turnaround is three business days,
so that would be a little tight for Saturday.
But we also offer a rush service that gets it done faster.
Though there's an extra fee for that.
The rush option sounds good, since I really can't miss the opening date.
Before I confirm the order though, could I take a look at the different types of paper you have?
I want to make sure I pick something that feels right.
Of course, that's a great idea.
Let me go and get our sample book so you can see all the options and compare them side by side.
Number 56.
Why is the man at the shop?
Number 57.
What does the woman say about the rush service?
Number 58.
What will the woman most likely do next?
Questions 59-61 refer to the following conversation.
Hi. I'm hoping to book a move for the 15th.
I've just signed for a new apartment across town, and that's the day I get the keys.
Let me check our schedule for you.
Oh, I'm sorry, but that whole week is already spoken for.
Oh, that's a problem.
The 15th is really the only day that works since my old lease ends then.
Well, I can send a crew out to you first thing the following morning instead.
That should still fit your timing.
That could work, thank you.
One more thing. Is there any chance you could help with the packing as well?
Of course.
Our packing service comes with all the boxes and wrapping materials you'll need.
Plus two staff to pack everything up for you.
Number 59.
Why is the man contacting the company?
Number 60.
What does the woman mean when she says that whole week is already spoken for?
Number 61.
What does the woman say about the packing service?
Question 62 through 64 refer to the following conversation and list.
Hi, I stopped in because I'd like to sign up for a new mobile data plan today.
I stream a lot of video on my phone, so I really need something that comes with plenty of data.
Of course, here at BrightWave Mobile, this is our list of plans and their monthly prices.
Since you use so much data, most people in your situation choose either the family plan
or the unlimited plan.
Let me take a look. I think the family plan will give me more than enough for what I need.
I'll go with that one.
Great. I'll get you enrolled right now and set up your new SIM card.
One more thing. I'd recommend turning on automatic payments so you never miss your monthly due date.
Number 62.
What is the woman shopping for?
Number 63.
Look at the graphic. How much will the woman pay per month?
Number 64.
What does the man recommend the woman do?
Question 65 through 67 refer to the following conversation and schedule.
Hi there. I'd like to book a sightseeing cruise with Seabright Harbour Cruises for this weekend.
Of course. Which day were you hoping to go out?
Saturday, please. I've got a lunch reservation booked for right afterward,
so an afternoon trip just wouldn't work for me.
Morning is a good choice actually.
There's a food festival on the waterfront this weekend,
and all of our afternoon cruises are filling up fast because of it.
Oh, that's lucky then. The morning slot suits me perfectly.
Great. Let me just check the schedule to see which boat you'll be sailing on that morning.
Sounds good. I'll take it.
Number 65.
Why does the man prefer the morning cruise?
Number 66.
What does the woman say is happening this weekend?
Number 67.
Look at the graphic. Which boat will the man most likely sail on?
Question 68 through 70 refer to the following conversation and map.
Hi. Good afternoon. I'm here for a two o'clock meeting with the Latham Group.
Could you tell me which room they're in?
Of course. Yes. I can see the booking right here.
The Latham Group has a room reserved for the whole afternoon on the second floor.
They're expecting a few visitors.
Great. One thing I'm carrying two heavy sample cases,
so I'd really like to avoid the stairs.
Is there an elevator I can use to get up there?
Absolutely. The elevator is right around the corner behind me.
When you come out on the second floor, the meeting room is directly across the corridor
from the cafe kiosk.
You can't miss it.
Number 68.
What does the man say about the meeting room?
Number 69.
What concern does the woman have?
Number 70.
Look at the graphic. Which room is the meeting in?
Part 4.
Directions.
You will hear some talks given by a single speaker.
You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speaker says in each talk.
Select the best response to each question and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet.
The talks will not be printed in your testbook and will be spoken only one time.
Question 71 through 73 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting.
Good morning, everyone, and thanks for getting here a little earlier than usual today.
The reason is that we've taken in a very large catering order for a wedding this weekend.
Three hundred pastries in total, and they all have to be finished by Saturday afternoon.
That means we need to work ahead.
So this morning, I'd like everyone to focus on mixing and shaping the dough before we start on our regular counter items.
The extra flour and butter were delivered last night, and you'll find them stacked in the back storage room right next to the mixers.
Please get your station set up and begin on the dough right away, because the first trays have to be in the oven by nine o'clock.
Let's keep things moving, and come find me if anything starts to run short.
Number 71.
What is the speaker mainly discussing?
Number 72.
What does the speaker ask the listeners to do?
Number 73.
By what time must the first trays be in the oven?
Question 74 through 76 referred to the following excerpt from a meeting.
Thanks everyone for coming in a little early this morning.
First, some good news.
The weekend loyalty promotion we ran last month brought in far more shoppers than we expected, and sales were up right across the store.
Because of that success, we're now introducing a new contactless checkout procedure starting this Saturday.
Honestly, our weekend afternoons already get very busy, so I've made some adjustments to next month's schedule.
I'd like each of you to practice the new steps at your own register by the end of this week.
You'll find the full written instructions in the binder in the break room, so please read through them before your next shift.
Let's make this a smooth change for our customers here at Brookvale Home and Living.
Number 74.
What good news does the speaker share at the start of the meeting?
Number 75.
What does the speaker imply when she says our weekend afternoons already get very busy?
Number 76.
What does the speaker ask the listeners to do by the end of the week?
Question 77 through 79 referred to the following broadcast.
And now for your evening traffic update.
Starting this Friday night, the Ardmore Bridge will be closed in both directions, so that crews can carry out some important repairs to the road surface.
The closure is expected to last all weekend, so drivers heading into the city centre should plan to use the Riverside Avenue crossing instead.
To help commuters who don't drive, the transit office will run a free shuttle bus between the two riverbanks every 20 minutes while the work is going on.
We expect the bridge to reopen to all traffic early Monday morning, so please allow yourself some extra time until then.
Number 77.
What is the broadcast mainly about?
Number 78.
What are drivers advised to do?
Number 79.
What does the speaker say will happen early Monday morning?
Questions 80 through 82 refer to the following tour information.
Welcome everyone, and thank you for joining our guided tour here at Tidewater Point.
The whole tour takes about 90 minutes, so we've got plenty to see together.
Before we start, I do need to ask one thing of you.
Please don't tap on the glass of any of the tanks, because it really startles the animals and can stress them out.
Alright, let's begin.
Our first stop will be the Coral Grove, where you'll see hundreds of small, brightly colored fish swimming among the reef.
From there, we'll move on to the Kelp Forest Gallery.
Now, at 2.30 this afternoon, there's a feeding presentation over in the Deep Reef Hall, so make a note of that time, because you'll really want to be back there for it.
It's the highlight of the whole visit.
Our tour will finish up near the main entrance, right by the gift shop, in case you'd like to pick up a souvenir on your way.
Okay, let's head over to the first exhibit.
Number 80.
Where most likely are the listeners?
Number 81.
According to the speaker, what will the listeners see first?
Number 82.
What does the speaker imply when he says, you'll really want to be back there for it?
Questions 83-85 refer to the following speech.
Good evening, everyone, and thank you so much for joining us here tonight.
I'm delighted to announce that, together, we have raised a remarkable $42,000 at this year's dinner.
None of this would have been possible without the incredible generosity of our local business sponsors, whose contributions truly carried us across the finish line.
Every dollar you've donated will go directly toward building a new playground and learning garden at the Fairhaven Community Center.
On behalf of the whole organizing team, I simply cannot thank you enough for supporting our neighborhood.
Now, please make your way through to the main hall, where our live auction is about to get underway.
Number 83.
Why is the speaker giving this talk?
Number 84.
What does the speaker say the money will be used for?
Number 85.
What are the listeners invited to do next?
Questions 86-88 refer to the following excerpt from an information session.
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to your first day orientation here at Elmwood Public Library.
I'm Colleen Whitfield, the staff coordinator.
The goal this morning is to give you everything you'll need before your very first shift at the front desk and out on the shelving floor.
In the folder we emailed you last week, you'll find the staff handbook and a shift schedule,
so please keep those close by throughout the session.
As part-time assistants, most of you will be working four-hour shifts, either in the morning or in the late afternoon.
Now, one quick correction.
Some of you were told to gather each day at the front counter, but from now on, your shifts will actually begin in the oak view room upstairs.
Please make a note of that because it takes effect starting this week.
Once we finish here, I'll take you on a walk through the whole building so you can see where everything is.
Number 86.
Who most likely are the listeners?
Number 87.
According to the speaker, what has been changed?
Number 88.
What will the speaker most likely do next?
Questions 89-91 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting.
Thanks for coming in early this morning, everyone, and welcome to our team meeting here at the Fenwood Grill.
I've called you together to let you know that our new auto menu will officially launch this coming Friday.
We've decided to introduce it because so many of our regular customers have been asking for warmer seasonal dishes,
and the local farms we work with have wonderful fresh produce available at this time of year.
The new menu will include three soups, two main courses, and a couple of desserts, all prepared with these seasonal ingredients.
So before Friday, I'd like each of you to attend the tasting session tomorrow afternoon and read carefully through the updated dish descriptions.
Number 89.
What is the talk mainly about?
Number 90.
Why is the restaurant introducing the new menu?
Number 91.
What are listeners asked to do?
Questions 92-94 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting.
Now, moving on to something that affects all of us.
Starting next month, our entire department will be relocating to the fourth floor of this building.
The company is renovating our current area to create additional meeting rooms,
so we all need to have our workspaces cleared out and ready to move by the end of the month.
I'd like each of you to pack up your own desk personally and clearly label every box with your name and team before you leave on the 28th.
You can pick up boxes, tape, and labels from the supply room next to the main entrance.
And if you have any questions about the move, please speak with Nathan Brooks, the facilities coordinator, who is organizing everything.
Number 92.
According to the speaker, what will happen next month?
Number 93.
What does the speaker ask listeners to do?
Number 94.
Who is Nathan Brooks?
Questions 95-97 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting and chart.
Good morning, everyone.
Just a quick meeting before we open the shop today.
If you look at this chart, you'll see the repair requests we handled this month, broken down by type of service.
The category we get the most requests for is clearly out ahead of the others.
So I've decided we'll hold a short skills session, focused on exactly that kind of repair.
I want to thank Bianca Fero for pulling all these records together, and putting the chart in order for us.
This training really matters, because when everyone can handle our busiest jobs quickly, customers wait less, and we get through the day more smoothly.
So please sign up for the session on the sheet by the front counter, before you leave on Thursday.
Number 95.
Look at the graphic, which service category will a training session focus on?
Number 96.
Why does the speaker thank Bianca Fero?
Number 97.
What does the speaker instruct the listeners to do?
Questions 98-100 refer to the following telephone message and list.
Hi, this is a message for Grace Whitlock.
This is Victor Salgado, calling from Ridley Alterations.
I'm just letting you know that your order is finished and ready to be picked up.
We shortened the hem on the gray jacket you brought in last week, and it turned out really nicely.
When you come by to collect it, please give the front desk the reference code for that service, so that we can find your item quickly.
I also wanted to mention that we're closing early this Friday, at 1 in the afternoon, for a staff meeting.
So if you're planning to come in on Friday, please call us back to confirm a pickup time before then.
Thanks, and we'll see you soon!
Number 98.
Why is the speaker calling?
Number 99.
Look at the graphic, which reference code should the listener give?
Number 100.
What does the speaker say will happen this Friday?
It's Friday!
